notes: A decision or sentence, here the verdict of death. In 1:9 Paul says that in Asia they felt they had received "the sentence of death," which made them depend on God who raises the dead. It appears only here in the New Testament.

elsewhere.note: We ourselves had the sentence of death within ourselves.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A deposit, the first installment of a payment, that guarantees the rest. It came into Greek from a Semitic word used in business deals. Paul says God gave "the Spirit in our hearts as a down payment" (1:22; 5:5), a pledge that more is coming.

elsewhere.note: Who is a pledge of our inheritance.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To close, mark, or authenticate with a seal, as an owner marked goods or a king authenticated documents. Paul says God "sealed us" (1:22), marking believers as his own.

elsewhere.note: God the Father has sealed him.
You were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise.
Until we have sealed the bondservants of our God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Singleness of purpose, without a double agenda, and so sincerity, and also generosity (giving without strings). Paul uses it for his sincerity (1:12; 11:3) and for the generosity of the Macedonians (8:2) and of the Corinthians' gift (9:11, 9:13).

elsewhere.note: He who gives, let him do it with generosity.
In singleness of your heart, as to Christ.
With singleness of heart, fearing the Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To be more than enough, to overflow. A favorite word in 2 Corinthians for abundance: of Christ's sufferings (1:5), comfort (1:5), joy (8:2), grace (9:8), and generosity (8:7).

elsewhere.note: The gift of grace abounded to the many.
I know how to abound.
My father's hired servants have bread enough to spare.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To lead in a victory procession, from which we get "triumph." In a Roman triumph, a victorious general paraded through the city with his captives. In 2:14 Paul says God "leads us in triumph in Christ," either as captives or sharers of the victory; scholars debate which he intends.

elsewhere.note: Having made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A smell, especially a sweet one (incense in a triumphal procession, or sacrifice). In 2:14-16 Paul says believers are "the aroma of Christ" to God: for those being saved, a fragrance of life, and for those perishing, a smell of death.

elsewhere.note: The house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
A fragrant aroma.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to peddle, to trade for profit
notes: To be a petty trader, especially a tavern keeper who dilutes wine to increase profit. Paul says he does not "peddle" God's word (2:17), unlike teachers who water it down for gain.

elsewhere.note: We are not as so many, peddling the word of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A letter of the alphabet, a written document, or the written law. In 3:6, "the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life" probably means the law as a written code, without the Spirit's power. Paul is not against Scripture; elsewhere he treasures it.

elsewhere.note: Circumcision is of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter.
In newness of the spirit and not in oldness of the letter.
If you don't believe his writings.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A covering, specifically a veil. In 3:12-18 Paul compares the veil Moses put on his face (Exodus 34:33-35) to a veil lying on the hearts of those who read Moses without Christ, and says the veil is removed in Christ.

elsewhere.note: The same veil remains on the reading of the old covenant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Freedom, the state of not being a slave. In 3:17, "where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty," a freedom connected to the removal of the veil. Paul uses it elsewhere for freedom from sin and the law (Romans 8:21; Galatians 5:1).

elsewhere.note: The glorious liberty of the children of God.
For freedom Christ has set us free.
Why is my liberty judged by another's conscience?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An image, likeness, or portrait, from which we get "icon." Paul says believers are being transformed into the image of the Lord (3:18), and calls Christ "the image of God" (4:4), who perfectly shows what God is like.

elsewhere.note: He is the image of the invisible God.
To be conformed to the image of his Son.
We will also bear the image of the heavenly.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: "We are transformed into the same image from glory to glory" (3:18).

elsewhere.note: Be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
He was transfigured before them.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to encourage, to exhort, to comfort
notes: To call alongside, to comfort, to urge. This is the key verb of the opening of the letter: God "comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction" (1:4), and Titus's arrival "comforted" Paul (7:6-7).

elsewhere.note: They shall be comforted.
With many other exhortations.
The one who exhorts, in his exhortation.
Who comforts us in all our affliction.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Comfort, encouragement. The noun appears about ten times in the first chapters: "the God of all comfort" (1:3-7), the comfort Paul received from Titus (7:4, 7:13), and the comfort of the Corinthians' change of heart.

elsewhere.note: You have received your consolation.
Barnabas, which means son of encouragement.
The God of all comfort.
If there is any encouragement in Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Pressure, affliction, trouble. Paul describes affliction in Asia (1:8), anguish of heart (2:4), and "our light affliction, which is for the moment" (4:17); the Macedonians gave despite "a great ordeal of affliction" (8:2).

elsewhere.note: Then there will be great tribulation.
In the world you have trouble.
Tribulation produces perseverance.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Grace, gift, favor. In this letter grace is both God's gift in Christ (8:9) and the word for the collection itself (8:4, 8:6-7, 9:8); in 12:9 the Lord says, "My grace is sufficient for you."

elsewhere.note: The Word was full of grace and truth.
The gospel of the grace of God.
By grace you are saved.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sharing, partnership. Paul speaks of sharing in Christ's sufferings and comfort (1:7), the sharing in the collection (8:4; 9:13), and asks, "What fellowship has light with darkness?" (6:14).

elsewhere.note: The fellowship.
The favor of taking part in the relief of the saints.
Your partnership in the gospel.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To give freely, to forgive. Paul asks the Corinthians to "forgive" the offender, and says he forgives too (2:7, 2:10); the related noun charis is behind much of this letter.

elsewhere.note: You should rather forgive and comfort him.
Forgiving each other, as God forgave you.
Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
Will he not also freely give us all things?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Grief, sorrow, pain. Paul writes of the grief his letter caused (2:1-7; 7:8-11), and distinguishes "godly grief," which leads to repentance, from "worldly grief," which leads to death (7:10).

elsewhere.note: He found them sleeping for sorrow.
I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish.
Godly grief produces repentance.
Sorrow upon sorrow.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A door. "A door was opened to me in the Lord" in Troas (2:12), as in Ephesus in 1 Corinthians 16:9.

elsewhere.note: Go into your room and shut the door.
The master has shut the door.
She came to answer the door.
I stand at the door and knock.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Good news, the gospel. Paul preaches it in Troas (2:12), says the gospel is veiled to those who are perishing (4:3-4), and speaks of the Corinthians' obedience to it (9:13).

range.note: News of a king's triumph or accession.
The message about Jesus, later also a name for books like Mark.

elsewhere.note: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The gospel I preached to you.
The gospel that was preached by me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to lose, to destroy, to perish
notes: To destroy, to perish. "Among those who are perishing" (2:15; 4:3), and "perplexed, but not despairing... struck down, but not destroyed" (4:8-9).

elsewhere.note: Go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Whoever believes in him will not perish.
The word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing.
Not wishing that any should perish.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to save, to heal, to make well
notes: To save, to rescue. "Among those who are being saved" (2:15); "now is the day of salvation" (6:2) comes from the same family.

range.note: To save from danger or death.
To save in the fullest sense.

elsewhere.note: He will save his people from their sins.
Everyone who calls will be saved.
By grace you are saved.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A covenant, a binding promise. Paul calls himself a minister "of a new covenant" (3:6) and speaks of the old covenant read aloud with a veil (3:14).

range.note: An agreement God makes with his people.
A document that gives an inheritance.

elsewhere.note: The blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
This cup is the new covenant in my blood.
The new covenant.
The mediator of a new covenant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Service, ministry. In 2 Corinthians the word is used for Paul's ministry (3:7-9; 4:1; 5:18; 6:3), for the collection (8:4; 9:1, 9:12-13), and for the opponents' claims (11:8).

elsewhere.note: Martha was distracted with much serving.
Whoever has a gift of service.
The ministry of reconciliation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to abolish, to bring to nothing
notes: To bring to an end, to make ineffective. In chapter 3 it describes the fading glory of the old covenant ministry, "which was passing away" (3:7, 3:11, 3:13-14).

elsewhere.note: Do we then nullify the law through faith?
Our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death.
That through death he might destroy him who had the power of death.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Glory. Chapter 3 contrasts the glory of the old and new covenant ministries, and says believers are being transformed "from glory to glory" (3:7-18); in 4:6 God's glory shines in the face of Christ.

elsewhere.note: They saw his glory.
The light of the knowledge of the glory of God.
He is the radiance of God's glory.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Spirit. In 2 Corinthians the Spirit is the one who writes on hearts (3:3), gives life (3:6), transforms (3:18), and is given as a down payment (1:22; 5:5); Paul ends with "the fellowship of the Holy Spirit" (13:14).

range.note: The Holy Spirit, or a spirit being.
Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.
Receive the Holy Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Lord. "Whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away" (3:16), and "we don't preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord" (4:5).

range.note: The title for God and for Jesus.

elsewhere.note: "Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord.'"
God has made him both Lord and Christ.
Every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Boldness, openness. "We use great boldness of speech" (3:12), and "our mouth is open to you" (6:11) from the same family of words.

elsewhere.note: He said this plainly.
No one who wants to be known openly acts in secret.
That I may boldly make known the mystery of the gospel.
Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to lose heart, to give up
notes: To grow weary or lose heart (from kakos, "bad"). In 4:1 and 4:16 Paul says, "we do not lose heart," and builds the whole chapter on why.

elsewhere.note: Always to pray and not to give up.
Let's not be weary in doing good.
I ask that you do not lose heart at my afflictions.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A treasure or the place where treasure is kept, from which we get "thesaurus," a treasury of words. In 4:7 the gospel is the treasure kept in clay jars.

range.note: A place where it is kept.

elsewhere.note: Don't lay up treasures on earth.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in the field.
In whom are all the treasures of wisdom.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Made of baked clay, like pottery. In 4:7 Paul says the treasure is held in "clay vessels," cheap, common, and fragile. The related word ostrakon means a broken piece of pottery.

elsewhere.note: Vessels of wood and clay.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A putting to death, or the state of being dead. In 4:10 Paul says he always carries "the dying of Jesus" in his body, so that Jesus' life may also be shown in him. The same word is used in Romans 4:19 for the deadness of Abraham's body.

elsewhere.note: The deadness of Sarah's womb.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To confine in a narrow space (stenos "narrow" plus chōros "space"). In 4:8, "pressed on every side, yet not crushed"; in 6:12 the Corinthians are "restricted" in their affections, not Paul.

elsewhere.note: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your own affections.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Darkness, literal and moral. In 4:6 God, who said "Light shall shine out of darkness," has shone in our hearts; in 6:14 Paul asks, "what communion has light with darkness?"

elsewhere.note: The people who sat in darkness saw a great light.
To turn them from darkness to light.
Who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To destroy, corrupt, or waste away thoroughly. In 4:16 "though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day."

elsewhere.note: Where no moth destroys.
A third of the ships were destroyed.
Men of corrupt minds.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Giving of light, enlightenment, from which we get "photo." In 4:4 and 4:6 Paul speaks of "the light of the gospel" and "the light of the knowledge of the glory of God." The word appears only in these two verses in the New Testament.

elsewhere.note: The light of the Good News of the glory of Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A tent, used as a picture of the body as a temporary home (5:1, 5:4). Related to skēnē, tent or tabernacle. Paul was a tentmaker (Acts 18:3).

range.note: The body as a temporary home.

elsewhere.note: While we are in this tent, we groan.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To groan, a deep sigh of longing or distress. In 5:2-4 Paul says that in this tent "we groan," longing for the heavenly dwelling; in Romans 8:23 creation and believers groan together.

range.note: Make a low sound of pain.

elsewhere.note: We ourselves groan within ourselves.
Looking up to heaven, he sighed.
So that they can do this with joy and not with groaning.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To put on a garment over another one. In 5:2-4 Paul longs to be "clothed over" with the heavenly dwelling, so that what is mortal is swallowed up by life, not to be found naked.

elsewhere.note: Not that we would be unclothed, but that we would be clothed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To be at home, in one's own place (en "in" plus dēmos "people, district"). Paul says that while we are at home in the body we are away from the Lord (5:6-9).

elsewhere.note: Rather be at home with the Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To be away from home, abroad (ek "out of" plus dēmos). In 5:6-9 Paul says that to be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord.

elsewhere.note: While we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: What is seen, the outward appearance or form. In 5:7, "we walk by faith, not by sight" (literally "by appearance").

elsewhere.note: In bodily form like a dove.
The appearance of his face was altered.
Abstain from every form of evil.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Creation, either the act of creating or what is created, a creature. In 5:17, "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation," which may also be read "there is a new creation."

elsewhere.note: The creation waits for the revealing of the children of God.
A new creation.
The firstborn of all creation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To act as an ambassador or envoy (from presbys, "elder"). Paul says believers are "ambassadors for Christ," pleading on his behalf, "be reconciled to God" (5:20; compare Ephesians 6:20).

elsewhere.note: For which I am an ambassador in chains.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To change from enmity to friendship, to reconcile. It was used in diplomacy and in marriage. Paul says God "reconciled us to himself through Christ" (5:18-20), and urges the Corinthians to be reconciled to God.

range.note: Change from one state to another.

elsewhere.note: We were reconciled to God through the death of his Son.
Let her be reconciled to her husband.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To walk about, and so to live or conduct oneself. Paul uses it for how a person lives: "we walk by faith, not by sight" (5:7); "not walking in craftiness" (4:2).

elsewhere.note: We also might walk in newness of life.
Walk by the Spirit.
Walk in love.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Well received, acceptable (eu "well" plus prosdechomai "to receive"). In 6:2, quoting Isaiah 49:8, "now is the acceptable time" (the time of God's favor), and in 8:12 a gift is acceptable if given willingly.

elsewhere.note: That the offering of the Gentiles might be acceptable.
Spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Labor that wears one out, toil. Paul lists "labors" among his hardships (6:5; 11:23, 11:27), and uses it for hard work in the Lord more broadly.

elsewhere.note: Your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
Your labor of love.
Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Going without sleep, a sleepless night. Paul lists "sleepless nights" among his hardships (6:5; 11:27).

elsewhere.note: In labor and travail, in watchings often.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Going without food, whether by choice (fasting) or necessity (hunger). Paul lists "hunger" or "fastings" among his hardships (6:5; 11:27).

elsewhere.note: Serving God with fastings and petitions night and day.
After prayer with fasting, they committed them to the Lord.
The Fast was already over.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Purity, moral cleanness. Paul lists purity among the signs of true ministry (6:6), and says he fears the Corinthians will be led away from "the simplicity and the purity" of devotion to Christ (11:3).

elsewhere.note: From the simplicity and the purity that is in Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be widened, to open wide
notes: To be made broad or wide (from platys, "broad"). In 6:11-13, Paul says "our heart is open wide," and asks the Corinthians to "open wide your hearts also."

elsewhere.note: They make their phylacteries broad.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The inner organs (heart, liver, lungs), thought of as the seat of strong emotion, so deep affection or compassion. In 6:12 the Corinthians are "restricted in your own affections," and in 7:15 Titus's affection grows toward them.

elsewhere.note: How I long for you all in the affection of Christ Jesus.
Put on a heart of compassion.
Closes his heart of compassion against him.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To be yoked with someone different (heteros "different" plus zygos "yoke"), as when two different animals are harnessed together. It appears only in 6:14, probably echoing Deuteronomy 22:10, where Israel was not to plow with an ox and donkey together.

elsewhere.note: Don't be unequally yoked with unbelievers.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A Hebrew word meaning "worthlessness" or "wickedness," used in Jewish writings as a name for a leader of evil. In 6:15, Paul asks, "What agreement has Christ with Belial?" It appears only here in the New Testament.

elsewhere.note: What agreement has Christ with Belial?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To enrich, to make wealthy. In 6:10 the apostles are "poor, yet making many rich"; in 9:11 the Corinthians are "enriched in everything" for generosity.

elsewhere.note: In everything you were enriched in him.
Being enriched in everything to all liberality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Haste, eagerness, diligence. In 7:11-12 Paul lists "what earnestness" godly sorrow produced in the Corinthians, and the word returns for the collection (8:7-8, 8:16-17, 8:22).

elsewhere.note: He who rules, with diligence.
Not lagging in diligence.
We desire that each one of you show the same diligence.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Strong desire, longing. In 7:7 and 7:11 Titus reports the Corinthians' "longing" for Paul, and Paul lists it among the fruits of godly grief. It appears only in this letter.

elsewhere.note: He told us your longing.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Putting right a wrong, either by avenging or vindicating. In 7:11 it is one of the fruits of godly grief: "what vindication" (or "what punishment"), meaning the Corinthians' readiness to put things right.

elsewhere.note: Won't God avenge his chosen ones?
Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay.
For vengeance on evildoers.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Staining or defilement, as of a stain on clothing. In 7:1, Paul urges them to "cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit." It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Let's cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The state of being holy, set apart for God. In 7:1, "perfecting holiness in the fear of God." Paul uses it for the process of becoming what God has set believers apart to be.

elsewhere.note: According to the Spirit of holiness.
So that he may establish your hearts blameless in holiness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Pure, free from stain, innocent. In 7:11, the Corinthians have shown themselves "pure" in the matter; in 11:2 Paul presents them to Christ as a "pure virgin."

elsewhere.note: Whatever things are pure.
Keep yourself pure.
The wisdom from above is first pure.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To work out, bring about, or produce. In 7:10-11 godly sorrow "produces" repentance, and in 4:17 "our light affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory."

elsewhere.note: Suffering produces perseverance.
Work out your own salvation.
Sin produced in me all kinds of coveting.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Light. God "who said, Light shall shine out of darkness" has shone in our hearts (4:6), Satan disguises himself as an angel of light (11:14), and Paul asks what fellowship light has with darkness (6:14).

elsewhere.note: You are the light of the world.
I am the light of the world.
God is light.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An age. "The god of this age" blinds the minds of the unbelieving (4:4).

elsewhere.note: "The harvest is the end of the age."
"The end of the age."
"In the ages to come."
Through whom he made the ages.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A vessel, jar, or tool. "We have this treasure in clay vessels" (4:7).

elsewhere.note: No one covers it with a jar.
Make one vessel for honorable use.
We have this treasure in jars of clay.
In a great house there are vessels of gold and silver.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To believe, trust. Paul quotes Psalm 116, "I believed, therefore I spoke," and says "we also believe, and therefore we also speak" (4:13).

elsewhere.note: Repent, and believe in the gospel.
Believe in the Lord Jesus.
If you believe in your heart.
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: eternal, of the age to come
notes: Eternal, lasting. "An eternal weight of glory" and "the things which are not seen are eternal" (4:17-18); a house "eternal in the heavens" (5:1).
uncertain: How to understand "eternal punishment" (25:46), as endless or as belonging to the age to come, has been debated across church history.

elsewhere.note: What good thing shall I do to have eternal life?
That whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
God gave us eternal life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A judgment seat, the raised platform from which a Roman official judged. "We must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ" (5:10).

elsewhere.note: They brought him to the judgment seat.
We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.

If their rejection means the reconciliation of the world.
